referral: Call 0151 218 7000 (lines are open Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 4:30 pm) or email merseyside@crisis.org.uk. You can also drop in Monday, Wednesday and Friday 09:30–12:30. Before you visit, they recommend you find out what Crisis can offer you in Merseyside and contact them by phone or email to discuss the best options. Crisis is not an emergency service. groups: People over the age of 16 who are experiencing homelessness, or immediately at risk of homelessness
facilities: Skylights can help in finding a home and settling in, finding work and applying for jobs, and looking after your health and wellbeing.
How we can help depends on your situation and needs. If another service can provide the support you need, we will refer you to them.

Get in touch so we can assess your situation and discuss next steps – this could lead to you becoming a Crisis member, which involves you being assigned a lead worker who will work with you over a few weeks or longer to help end your homelessness.

Our Engagement and Assessment team will assess your initial support needs. We'll provide you with information, advice and guidance and create a plan with you around how we can support you to sustainably end your homelessness.
We can support you to access our Learning and Skills support that includes Tenancy skills, Budgeting, Property Pool, Job Club and digital literacy.
We also provide a Coaching service to offer longer term support to people to work towards achieving their goals and to address any areas that may be contributing to their homelessness.
Our work is supported by clinical psychologists, housing law specialists as well as Volunteering and Events teams.
Crisis does not offer emergency services.
Bathrooms at Crisis Skylight Merseyside are gender neutral.
